title: Open Day
tagline: Run a whole school day, fix one thing, and choose the right materials.
grownUp: This mission brings the whole school together for one day: bells, lessons, lunch and the report. The Architect watches what works and fixes one thing.
The materials story and the Big Question are about warmth, light and strength. Let the Architect give reasons, and say that different buildings choose different materials.
The bridge test is safe to try at home with household things. Stop as soon as anything bends or wobbles, and keep the books on a sturdy table.

steps.title: What is it made of?
steps.text: Architects choose materials carefully. Wood feels warm, glass lets light in, and stone is strong and lasts a long time.
steps.ask: Which material do you like the look of most, and why?

steps.title: Wood, glass or stone?
steps.scenario: What should the aquarium arch be made of?

options.label: Wood
options.detail: It feels warm and friendly, and it can be shaped into a smooth curve.

options.label: Glass
options.detail: Light pours in and you can see the fish from outside, but glass can feel cold and shows every fingerprint.

options.label: Stone
options.detail: It is very strong and lasts a long time, but it is heavy and can feel cold.

steps.reveal: Architects weigh up warmth, light, strength and how long a material will last. Real buildings use all three, and each choice gives something different.
steps.followUp: Which material would make your aquarium feel the most like a special place, and why?

steps.title: Which bridge holds most books?
need: A piece of card, like a cereal box
A pile of books, with a grown-up
steps: Lay the card across two stacks of books, with a gap between the stacks. Add books on top one at a time.
Do the same with the wooden ruler, then the plastic ruler, across the same gap.
Stop as soon as a bridge bends or slips. Count the books on each one, and talk about which material held the most.
steps.why: Architects test materials to see which ones are strong enough, and the answer can surprise you.
